title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
abstract: arXiv:2611.17563v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A benchmark usually measures a language model alone with a question, and deployment rarely looks like that: answers get contested, and models give up correct ones under counter-reasoning that is itself wrong. We show that what fails there is not a shortfall of accuracy but a capability in its own right -- knowing when to hold a position and when to yield to a better one -- which we call dialectical competence. It stands on first-answer accuracy without following from it: a model can be made materially better at answering and no better at this, and training for accuracy alone can drift against it. Nor can it be bought at inference, by self-reflection or by sampling more. Taking a cue from the dialectical tradition in philosophy, in which productive opposition arises within a position rather than being imposed on it from outside, we hypothesize that this capability can be trained from opposition the model supplies itself. translated_title: 基准测试不会反驳你：在自我分歧中学习
translated_abstract: 基准测试通常是让语言模型独自面对一个问题，而实际部署中很少出现这样的情形：答案会受到质疑，模型会在本身错误的反驳推理下放弃原本正确的答案。我们证明，在这种情形下失效的并非准确率的不足，而是一种独立存在的能力——知道何时坚持立场、何时向更优的立场让步——我们将其称为辩证能力。这种能力以首次回答的准确率为基础，但并不由其必然导出：可以显著提升模型的回答水平却对这种能力毫无帮助，而仅针对准确率的训练甚至会使其发生退化。这种能力也无法在推理阶段通过自我反思或增加采样次数来获得。借鉴哲学中的辩证传统——其中富有成效的对立产生于立场内部，而非从外部强加——我们假设这种能力可以通过模型自身提供的对立观点来进行训练。它提出一个立场……
tldr: 该论文提出“辩证能力”这一概念——即知道何时坚持立场、何时向更优答案让步的能力，证明其无法通过准确率训练或推理时的自我反思获得，而应借鉴哲学辩证法思想，通过模型自身生成的对立观点进行训练。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "dialectical competence" — knowing when to hold a position and when to yield to a better one — showing it cannot be gained through accuracy training or inference-time self-reflection, but can be trained from the model's own self-supplied opposition, inspired by the philosophical dialectical tradition.
